items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: Was it Dane at 26? No, I know it was in 26.

ctx.x: Yeah. Down in Our Alley Blues, did those come up? So Lova Queek? No. All right. Yeah, that's one of them. Well, you know, that's the way you come into the band earlier than I thought. You know, that's what I was asking, I got the book.

Yeah, well, you must have it by, that must be Bass Headwood. It might be. Yeah. It might be a couple times. How far back is it? I can tell you exactly. Well, I joined Dugaldon Band in 26. I made the records from 26 up until 35. Was it Dane at 26? No, I know it was in 26. From that until 35.

See, now he made East St. Louis Tudeloo and Birmingham Breakdown, Fort Brunswick, February 28, 1927. I remember that. That's why I can tell you. Yeah, that would be after you could join the band. Did you ever make New Orleans Lowdown and Song of the Cotton Feet? I remember them by that name.
